title: September 30, 1989: India launched a submarine it had never built before - and built it anyway.
caption:
September 30, 1989: India launched a submarine it had never built before - and built it anyway.

It was India's first indigenously built submarine - a Shishumar-class diesel-electric vessel, built under a technology transfer agreement with Germany's HDW, but fabricated entirely in India. Construction had begun in 1984.

Raw materials like HY-80 high-strength steel came from abroad, but all cutting, forming and welding on INS Shalki was done domestically - a genuine fabrication milestone, not just assembly. It was commissioned into active Indian Navy service on February 7, 1992, over two years after its launch.

A Viksit Bharat by 2047 needs the industrial base to build what it can't buy. INS Shalki is the quiet, unglamorous starting point for the indigenous defense manufacturing capability India leans on today.
